title: Scheme atlas for a quasi-Deligne--Mumford algebraic stack
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic stacks mean [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], fibred groupoids and $2$-fibre products mean [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A representable map is representable by algebraic spaces; its local quasi-finiteness means local quasi-finiteness after every scheme base change on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Flatness and local finite presentation of representable maps are likewise tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $\mathcal X/S$ be an algebraic stack. Its diagonal $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}$ is locally quasi-finite if and only if there are a scheme $W/S$ and a representable morphism $q:W\to\mathcal X$ which is surjective, flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite. Surjectivity means that every object of $\mathcal X$ over a field acquires, after a field extension, a lift to $W$ together with an isomorphism of its image with that object. No separatedness, quasi-compactness, Noetherianity, or finite-inertia hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06MF (theorem-quasi-DM), equivalence (1)--(2); relative over S, as in the chapter conventions; quasi-DM expanded as locally quasi-finite diagonal.

proof.text: Assume the atlas $q:W\to\mathcal X$ exists. The $2$-fibre product $\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack by the fibre-product lemma, and $W\times_SW$ is a scheme. The map $W\times_SW\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation: factor it as two base changes of $q$. The pullback of $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}$ to this cover is $j:W\times_{\mathcal X}W\to W\times_SW$. Its composite with the first projection to $W$ is a base change of $q$, hence locally quasi-finite. Left cancellation for algebraic spaces makes $j$ locally quasi-finite. The fppf target test then gives local quasi-finiteness of the diagonal.

source.place: Tag 06MF, (2) implies (1), expanded proof of Tag 06MB (lemma-properties-covering-imply-diagonal), (2).

proof.text: Conversely assume $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}$ locally quasi-finite. Fix a finite-type point $x$. Choose the affine smooth chart $U\to\mathcal X$, closed $u\in U$, $k=\kappa(u)$ and locally finite type field self-groupoid $R=u\times_{\mathcal X}u$ supplied by the closed-chart lemma. Put $F=U\times_{\mathcal X}u$. This is an algebraic space smooth over $k$. All maps from these scheme or space sources to $\mathcal X$ are representable by its representable diagonal.

Let $G=R\times_{u\times_Su}u$ be the stabilizer of this field groupoid. Its objects are automorphisms of the chosen object over $u$, so $G=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X}u$. Thus $G\to u$ is locally quasi-finite by base change of the diagonal. For every etale scheme chart $V\to G$, the scheme map $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally quasi-finite by the chart definition. The scheme relative-dimension-zero criterion gives $\dim_vV=0$ for every $v$; hence $\dim G=0$ by the chart definition of space dimension. The field-groupoid dimension lemma yields $\dim R=\dim G=0$. The identity $e:u\to R\to F$ gives a $k$-rational point $z$ with $p(z)=u$, and the defining square identifies $R$ with $F\times_Uu$.

source.place: Tag 06MF, field groupoid and stabilizer paragraph.

proof.text: Apply the smooth-fibre parameter lemma to $p:F\to U$ and $z$. Its hypotheses hold: $F/k$ is smooth, $u$ is closed, $z$ is $k$-rational with $k=\kappa(u)$, and its $p$-fibre $R$ is zero-dimensional. It gives functions $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ on an affine neighbourhood $U'$ of $u$, regular at a point of an etale chart above $z$, and $Z=V(f_1,\ldots,f_d)$ with $z\in Z\times_{\mathcal X}u$ and $\dim_z(Z\times_{\mathcal X}u)=0$. The restriction $U'\to\mathcal X$ of the smooth chart to the affine neighbourhood $U'$ is smooth by open-source locality, hence flat and locally of finite presentation, and the etale chart lies over its field fibre $U'\times_{\mathcal X}u=p^{-1}(U')$. Apply the stack regular-slice flatness lemma to $U'\to\mathcal X$ and these functions; after shrinking around $u$, $Z\to\mathcal X$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. This shrinking retains $z$ and the dimension-zero conclusion.

source.place: Tag 06MF, local-ring and regular-slice paragraph, using Tag 06MD.

proof.text: Local finite presentation gives local finite type for $Z\to\mathcal X$. Apply the fibre-neighbourhood lemma to the dimension-zero point $z$ of its fibre over $u$. Restrict $Z$ to the resulting open neighbourhood of $u$. The resulting scheme $Z_x$ still maps over $x$ and is locally quasi-finite, flat and locally of finite presentation over $\mathcal X$; flatness and local finite presentation persist on this open source restriction.

source.place: Tag 06MF, end of slice paragraph, using Tag 06ME.

proof.text: Choose one such $Z_x$ for each finite-type point and form the scheme $W=\coprod_x Z_x$. This family is indexed by a set of the chosen universe: fix one smooth surjective scheme atlas $U_0\to\mathcal X$; by field-extension lifting every point of $|\mathcal X|$ is the image of a point of $U_0$, so choosing such a point for each finite-type point embeds the index set into $|U_0|$. Each $Z_x$ is a scheme of the site, so the coproduct is a scheme in the chosen universe. The maps glue to an object over $W$ because the summands form a disjoint open cover and $\mathcal X$ is a stack. The representable-diagonal lemma makes $q:W\to\mathcal X$ representable. By open-source locality, $q$ is flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite. Its image contains every finite-type point, so the flat-lfp finite-type-surjectivity lemma makes $q$ surjective. If $\mathcal X$ is empty, the empty family gives the empty scheme and the same conclusion.
